pin.longFormSummary:
A budget hotel and hostel hybrid beside Dresden’s main station, with private family rooms, a guest kitchen, shared spaces and music-inspired interiors.

Family and budget stay

Book a whole private family room and confirm beds, occupancy and cot needs. Dormitory beds are separate products. The guest kitchen, game zone and lounge support longer stays and time between outings; check equipment, storage and house rules. Music-inspired decoration includes disco balls in guestrooms.

The station-side location supports rail travel and city exploring. Plan walking or tram routes to the historic centre, especially with children or luggage. Compare the full private-room price, taxes, breakfast, parking, luggage storage and cancellation terms for your dates.

Guest feedback

Guests value the station access, while accounts raise housekeeping, replenishment of essentials, paid luggage storage, service and value concerns. Both private-room and dormitory feedback merit attention. These are guest reports; confirm cleaning arrangements and accessibility for the exact room. The rubric is a dated snapshot with a small review sample, and retains the lower cleanliness score.

Opening and capacity

The hotel opened on 14 September 2022, as reported that day by Radio Dresden. The grocery store in the same building had opened earlier; its date is not used for the hotel.

The launch release reports 173 rooms and 719 beds. These opening-era figures replace earlier planned capacities. No hotel-specific construction investment was verified; the mixed-use building’s cost is not allocated to this hotel.

Small sample, housekeeping, supplies, storage fees and value concerns explicit. MICHELIN complete Dresden list 1–9 of 9 has no MEININGER match; Forbes Dresden unavailable; AAA excludes Germany. Acclaim null due guide gap.

pin.longFormSummary:
A family resort near Williamsburg, Virginia, with suites, overnight indoor water-park access, daily family activities and additional paid attractions.

Family water-park stay

Choose the exact suite layout, beds and booked occupancy; standard, themed, loft and larger suites have different limits. Overnight water-park access and daily family activities are included. Confirm operating hours, height restrictions, wristbands, supervision and arrival-day or departure-day access.

Paid attractions, dining, parking and other extras can add to the bill. Compare the complete stay price and package terms for the actual dates. Historic Triangle visits are separate outings: plan driving times, admission and attraction calendars.

Guest feedback

Families praise the water park, activities and some helpful staff. Accounts also report cleaning and maintenance concerns, inconsistent service, booking-price disputes and extra parking costs. These are guest accounts; review current suite-specific feedback and confirm the full bill. Component scores are a dated available-page snapshot rather than live ratings.

AAA’s exact-property inspector profile describes family lofts, kids’ cabin suites and fireplaces, and lists 405 units. Confirm which features are included in the booked suite.

Opening and original resort development

The operator’s shareholder letter explicitly dates the original opening to 23 March 2005, with 301 suites and 66,000 square feet of indoor entertainment space. Entertainment space includes more than the water park. Those are opening-era figures, separate from later expansion.

The 2005 hotel-waterpark construction report records US$48 million in total cost for the original Williamsburg resort. This is a reported historical project cost, distinct from earlier proposals, later expansion budgets and nightly rates.

The current operator profile lists 405 suites across 13 suite types. Check the exact category and occupancy rather than assuming every suite has the same beds, kitchen facilities or accessibility.
